punchline: Engineers who saw the foam hit Columbia's wing asked for images, and the request was cancelled in about ninety minutes.
thirty_sec: Edmondson uses the 2003 Columbia disaster as a case of silence. Foam struck the shuttle's wing at launch, and engineers wanted better images. A request was cancelled, and the engineer who led the debris team later said he regretted not speaking up at the meeting. Columbia broke apart on reentry, and all seven astronauts died. She stresses that this is not unique to NASA.
